ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows x-y coordinate axes in units of meters, with the positive charge Q marked near the origin, carrying a positive sign; the observation point (2,0) is marked on the positive direction of the x-axis, located to the right of Q. Reasoning: Since Q is a positive charge, the direction of the electric field it produces at the point (2,0) on the right side is along the +x direction, and its magnitude is kQ/2^2. The new charge q is also a positive charge, and can be placed at any position in the region. If q is placed to the left of (2,0), for example between the origin and (2,0), or to the left of the origin, then the electric field produced by q at (2,0) also points to the right, in the same direction as Q's electric field, so the resultant electric field strength increases. If q is placed to the right of (2,0), then the electric field produced by q at (2,0) points to the left, opposite to Q's electric field; if q is placed far enough away so that its opposite electric field is smaller than the original electric field of Q, then the magnitude of the resultant electric field will be smaller than before. Therefore |E| can increase or decrease depending on the position of q.
